newsitem.title: BELGIUM: U.S. TOBACCO RULING SEEN SPURRING BELGIAN AD BAN.
newsitem.headline: U.S. TOBACCO RULING SEEN SPURRING BELGIAN AD BAN.

text.p: The landmark admission by a U.S. tobacco company that smoking is addictive and can damage health was on Friday welcomed by Belgian politicians seeking an outright ban on tobacco advertising and sponsorship.

In the harshest blow yet to the cigarette industry, the U.S. Liggett Group agreed Thursday to settle tobacco litigation with almost half of the nation's attorneys general and hand over documents potentially devastating for the whole industry.
"I think this is an important step forward," Myriam Vanlerberghe, a member of the Belgian parliament and main sponsor of the tobacco ad ban bill, told Reuters.
"I hope that now (the opponents of my bill) will see that it's not really good to listen to the cigarette industry lobby."
The bill has already been adopted once by the chamber of deputies, the lower house in Belgium's Parliament, but has run into stiff opposition in the Senate, the upper house.

Senators from the region surrounding Belgium's famous Spa-Francorchamps Grand Prix circuit are seeking to amend the bill to preserve the race on the grounds that tobacco sponsorship is needed to cover the huge costs of staging such events.

Vanlerberghe said she expected the parliament's health committee, which she chairs, would resist all efforts to weaken the legislation. "If we open the door to Francorchamps, we will open the door for a lot of other events," she said.
Belgium's Senate has just two weeks to adopt its amendments before a 60-day parliamentary guillotine falls on the bill. If it fails to modify the bill, it will automatically become law.
